title: Build a balanced plate
suggestion: Try half a plate of vegetables, a quarter of protein such as dal, beans, tofu, eggs or fish, and a quarter of whole grains.
contextNotes: Adapt portions and food choices to your prescribed meal plan; kidney disease may need different protein and mineral targets.

title: Make one whole-grain swap
suggestion: Swap a refined grain for oats, whole-wheat roti or another whole grain you enjoy.

title: Add another vegetable
suggestion: Add a vegetable to lunch or dinner and vary the colors across the week.
contextNotes: Follow any kidney-related potassium restrictions.

title: Try a bean or lentil meal
suggestion: Include dal, chickpeas or beans in a meal for plant protein and fibre.
contextNotes: Portion and potassium needs can differ with kidney disease.

title: Include a protein food
suggestion: Add an appropriate portion of lentils, tofu, eggs, fish or another protein food to a meal.
contextNotes: Ask your dietitian about protein portions if you have kidney disease; this is not a high-protein prescription.

title: Choose an unsaturated fat
suggestion: Use a small amount of olive, canola or another unsaturated oil instead of butter when cooking.

title: Add nuts or seeds thoughtfully
suggestion: Try a small serving of unsalted nuts or seeds as part of a balanced meal or snack.
contextNotes: Choose an allergy-safe option. Kidney-related potassium and phosphorus restrictions may change suitable choices.

title: Build fibre gradually
suggestion: Add whole grains, vegetables or legumes gradually rather than changing everything at once.

title: Make water easy to reach
suggestion: Keep water available and drink regularly through the day, following your own fluid needs.
contextNotes: Do not use a universal three-litre target. Kidney disease, prescribed fluid limits and other medical needs require an individual plan.

title: Choose a drink without added sugar
suggestion: Choose water or an unsweetened drink instead of a sugary drink.
contextNotes: Do not substitute this for the fast-acting carbohydrate in your prescribed low-glucose treatment plan.

title: Flavor food with less salt
suggestion: Try herbs and spices for flavor, and choose lower-sodium packaged foods.
contextNotes: Check before using potassium-based salt substitutes, especially with kidney disease or medicines that affect potassium.

title: Explore a heart-friendly meal pattern
suggestion: Use a DASH-style pattern with vegetables, whole grains and suitable protein foods, adjusted to your needs.
contextNotes: A kidney condition or prescribed nutrition plan may need modifications.

title: Give your meal your attention
suggestion: Put your phone aside, slow down and notice flavor and fullness while eating.

title: Start with a comfortable portion
suggestion: Serve a comfortable portion first, then pause and check whether you are still hungry before taking more.
contextNotes: Avoid restrictive portions when underweight, pregnant or following a clinician-directed nutrition plan.

title: Plan a satisfying snack
suggestion: When hungry between meals, plan a snack such as fruit with unsweetened yogurt or another suitable whole-food combination.
contextNotes: Meal count alone does not make an eating pattern unhealthy. Keep medically required snacks and match choices to allergies, glucose management and kidney restrictions.

title: Plan dinner with sleep in mind
suggestion: Try a lighter dinner a few hours before bed instead of a large late-evening meal.
contextNotes: Use your bedtime rather than a fixed 7 pm cutoff. Follow prescribed meal and snack timing, especially with insulin.

title: Leave a gap before lying down
suggestion: If reflux bothers you during sleep, finish your meal at least three hours before lying down.
contextNotes: Use a diabetes-safe meal plan if you need a prescribed bedtime snack.

title: Notice your reflux triggers
suggestion: Note foods or drinks that reliably worsen your heartburn, then discuss practical swaps with your clinician.
contextNotes: Avoid eliminating whole food groups without a clear reason.

title: Review recent habit changes
suggestion: Review meal patterns, movement and sleep alongside your recent weight change, and choose one sustainable adjustment.
contextNotes: Weight changes can have several causes. Review what changed before deciding whether weight loss is right for you.

title: Choose a sustainable weight plan
suggestion: If weight management is appropriate for you, ask for a plan built around balanced meals, movement and sleep.
contextNotes: Adult BMI is an evaluation measure, not a diagnosis. Pregnancy, unintended weight change and eating-disorder history need tailored advice; neck size alone does not justify weight loss.

title: Keep a steady wake time
suggestion: Choose a consistent wake time and keep it similar on weekdays and weekends.

title: Set a wind-down reminder
suggestion: Set a reminder to start winding down, allowing enough time for your planned sleep.

title: Protect time for sleep
suggestion: Protect a regular sleep window instead of letting chores or screens push bedtime later.
contextNotes: The reported uninterrupted-sleep value is not a measurement of total sleep need. Persistent fatigue needs review even with adequate time in bed.

title: Choose a quiet wind-down
suggestion: Try reading, a warm bath or a relaxing activity as you get ready for bed.

title: Dim screens before bed
suggestion: Lower screen brightness and put screens aside during your wind-down.

title: Make your sleep space restful
suggestion: Keep your sleep space dark, quiet and comfortably cool.

title: Move caffeine earlier
suggestion: If you use caffeine, move it earlier in the day and notice whether your sleep improves.
contextNotes: Caffeine is not a substitute for sleep or a way to make drowsy driving safe.

title: Try a comfortable side position
suggestion: If comfortable and safe for you, try sleeping on your side rather than your back.
contextNotes: Side sleeping does not replace evaluation for breathing pauses. Adapt to mobility limitations and clinician advice.

title: Bring a sleep diary
suggestion: Record sleep times, awakenings and daytime sleepiness to share at your next appointment.

title: Take a quiet pause
suggestion: Try a few comfortable breaths or a short guided relaxation, without holding your breath or forcing it.
contextNotes: This is a relaxation habit, not treatment for thyroid disease, oxygen deficiency or sleep apnea. Stop if you feel uncomfortable or dizzy.

title: Make room for comfortable movement
suggestion: Choose a manageable walk, wheeling session or another activity you enjoy and build up gradually.
contextNotes: Use your care-team activity plan with heart or lung disease, stroke history, neuromuscular disorders or mobility limits.

title: Break up sitting
suggestion: During a long seated period, take a brief movement break that fits your ability.
contextNotes: Movement may help you feel refreshed, but ongoing sleepiness still needs evaluation.

title: Support strength as you age
suggestion: If suitable for you, include strength and balance activities alongside regular movement.
contextNotes: Choose supervised or adapted exercises if balance, mobility or medical conditions make this difficult.

title: Try comfortable movement after a meal
suggestion: If your care plan allows it, choose an easy walk or another comfortable activity after a meal.
contextNotes: Insulin and some diabetes medicines can cause low glucose with activity; follow your meal and glucose plan.

title: Plan your exercise recovery
suggestion: After activity, return to your usual balanced meal or snack plan and hydrate within your own fluid allowance.
contextNotes: Use prescribed glucose monitoring with insulin; do not force fluids or add protein supplements automatically.

title: Coordinate meal timing with medicines
suggestion: Ask your diabetes team how to fit meals, snacks and activity around your medicines.
contextNotes: Do not skip or delay prescribed meals or change insulin doses independently.

title: Agree an activity and glucose plan
suggestion: Before changing exercise, agree when to check glucose and how to handle lows with your diabetes team.
contextNotes: Do not alter insulin doses based on this suggestion.

title: Review your HbA1c in context
suggestion: Discuss your HbA1c result and an individualized food, activity and follow-up plan with your clinician.
contextNotes: Your clinician can interpret your HbA1c result alongside your medical history and agree on a personal target.

title: Choose sustainable PCOS habits
suggestion: Build enjoyable movement and balanced meals into your routine, alongside your clinician-led PCOS care.
contextNotes: Healthy habits can be useful without weight loss; avoid blanket low-carbohydrate or high-protein prescriptions.

title: Discuss thyroid care and supplements
suggestion: Keep a balanced eating pattern and check any thyroid-support or iodine supplement with your care team.
contextNotes: Lifestyle changes do not replace thyroid medicines or thyroid testing.

title: Personalize your kidney nutrition plan
suggestion: Ask a renal dietitian about the right fluid, protein, sodium, potassium and phosphorus choices for you.
contextNotes: Follow your kidney care team's personal guidance on fluids, protein and potassium.

title: Arrange a breathing-pause evaluation
suggestion: Tell a healthcare professional about observed pauses in breathing during sleep and ask about sleep evaluation.

title: Discuss persistent daytime sleepiness
suggestion: Bring persistent sleepiness, unrefreshing sleep or repeated awakenings to your healthcare professional.

title: Do not drive when sleepy
suggestion: If you feel sleepy, do not drive; arrange another way to travel and discuss the sleepiness with your clinician.

title: Discuss sleep alongside heart care
suggestion: Tell your care team about sleep concerns alongside your heart, circulation or blood-pressure history.
contextNotes: Your care team can assess heart or circulation symptoms and advise on next steps.

title: Review breathing and sleep together
suggestion: Discuss breathing concerns during sleep with the team managing your lung condition.
contextNotes: Do not change oxygen, inhalers or breathing-device settings from wellness advice.

title: Mention sleep concerns before procedures
suggestion: Before a procedure, tell the team about prior anesthesia complications and any known or suspected sleep apnea.

title: Ask for an adapted activity plan
suggestion: Ask your care team which movement and sleep-support habits suit your neuromuscular condition.
contextNotes: Avoid unsupervised exercise or breathing exercises that exceed your ability.

title: Record headaches alongside sleep
suggestion: Note headache timing and your sleep pattern, and share recurring headaches with your clinician.
contextNotes: Headaches have many causes. Ask your clinician to help identify the cause if they persist.

title: Discuss repeated waking to urinate
suggestion: Record awakenings to urinate and discuss them alongside your sleep and other symptoms.
contextNotes: Do not restrict fluids aggressively or change diuretics independently.

title: Mention sleep concerns during eye care
suggestion: Keep your eye-care follow-up and mention any breathing pauses or daytime sleepiness you have noticed.
contextNotes: Sleep habits do not replace glaucoma treatment or eye-pressure monitoring.

title: Use a pregnancy-aware wellness plan
suggestion: Discuss sleep and nutrition with your maternity or usual care team if you have a history of pregnancy-related complications.
contextNotes: These questions record history, not current pregnancy status. Do not prescribe weight loss or restrictive meal plans from this history.

title: Include sleep in your care conversation
suggestion: Mention sleep and daytime energy concerns when discussing infertility or erectile dysfunction with your clinician.
contextNotes: Discuss possible causes with your clinician before taking hormones or supplements.

title: Bring snoring to your next check-in
suggestion: Discuss persistent loud snoring with your healthcare professional, especially with sleepiness or breathing pauses.

title: Ask about adequate nourishment
suggestion: If your adult BMI is below 18.5, ask for help meeting your nutrition needs rather than reducing portions.
contextNotes: Adult BMI cutoffs do not apply to children or pregnancy; low BMI alone does not establish a diagnosis.

title: Understand a decrease in weight
suggestion: If your weight has dropped, check whether it was intended and discuss an unexplained drop with your clinician.
contextNotes: If your weight loss was unexpected, discuss it with your clinician before trying to lose more weight.
